source.book: 《史记》卷一百零五《扁鹊仓公列传》
source.excerpt: 文帝四年中，人上書言意，以刑罪當傳西之長安。意有五女，隨而泣。意怒，罵曰：「生子不生男，緩急無可使者！」於是少女緹縈傷父之言，乃隨父西。上書曰：「妾父為吏，齊中稱其廉平，今坐法當刑。妾切痛死者不可復生而刑者不可復續，雖欲改過自新，其道莫由，終不可得。妾願入身為官婢，以贖父刑罪，使得改行自新也。」書聞，上悲其意，此歲中亦除肉刑法。
source.transcriptionNote: 复用现有已录入批次的逐字原文快照；底本定位、原件哈希及行号保留。电子本尚不宣称纸本异文全校。

panels.title: 父亲将受刑
panels.caption: 淳于意因案将被送往长安，面临刑罚。
panels.scene: Mature Chunyu Yi stands beside an official at departure gate, plain travel bundle, worried expression, no chains or injury.

panels.title: 女儿们哭了
panels.caption: 他的五个女儿哭着相随。
panels.scene: Exactly FIVE daughters in plain robes stand with father, youngest adult Tiying in rust-red nearest him; others muted ochre, green, gray, cream.

panels.title: 一句伤心的话
panels.caption: 淳于意生气地说：“生了女儿，没有儿子，遇到急事竟没有可依靠的人！”
panels.scene: Father speaks in frustration; adult Tiying looks hurt but attentive. Keep all human and restrained, no threatening gestures.

evidence.excerpt: 生子不生男，緩急無可使者

panels.title: 她决定同行
panels.caption: 缇萦为父亲的话难过，却没有停在哭泣里。她跟随父亲，向长安而去。
panels.scene: Tiying in rust-red walks beside father on ancient road toward distant city, same adult face and clothes, light travel bundle.

panels.title: 写下一封上书
panels.caption: 缇萦向皇帝上书，为父亲请求改过的机会。
panels.scene: Tiying kneels at a low desk preparing a plain bamboo petition; focus on determined expression, brush strokes not visible or readable.

panels.title: 刑伤不能复原
panels.caption: 她说，死者不能复生，受损的身体也难恢复；即使想改过，也失去了机会。
panels.scene: Close portrait of Tiying speaking earnestly as narrator visual, holding closed petition roll; no mutilation, no imagined wounded people.

evidence.excerpt: 死者不可復生而刑者不可復續

panels.title: 愿意代父赎罪
panels.caption: “我愿入官府为婢，替父亲赎罪，让他能够改过自新。”
panels.scene: Tiying respectfully offers the CLOSED petition to an imperial clerk at palace entrance. No servitude scene: this is only her request.

evidence.excerpt: 妾願入身為官婢，以贖父刑罪

panels.title: 皇帝读到了
panels.caption: 上书传到汉文帝面前，文帝为她的心意悲悯感动。
panels.scene: Emperor Wen in burgundy thoughtfully reads plain unmarked bamboo petition in palace, expression compassionate, no direct meeting with Tiying invented.

panels.title: 刑制发生变化
panels.caption: 《史记》接着记载，这一年，朝廷也废除了肉刑法。
panels.scene: Emperor consults several officials with closed bamboo legal rolls on table, indicating deliberation and order. No modern proclamation or readable text.

panels.title: 留下她的声音
panels.caption: 故事里，被父亲认为难以依靠的女儿，勇敢地说出了自己的请求。
panels.scene: Final quiet portrait of adult Tiying holding a closed petition roll, steady hopeful expression against restrained ancient city backdrop. No father release or reunion shown.

adaptations: 缇萦年龄未载，按未标具体年龄的年轻女子表现，不称幼童或具体岁数。
本人自请为婢与刑制变化分别表达；不补无罪判决、实际服婢、父女团聚或全国欢庆。
保留本传纪年与通鉴异记，不把两书时间静默拼成一致。

generation.prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: a finished Histree vintage Chinese lianhuanhua story atlas, exactly 10 sequential illustrations on ONE image. Primary request: 缇萦上书救父. Composition: STRICT equal rectangular grid of TWO columns and 5 rows. Read left to right, top to bottom. All row heights equal, all column widths equal. Canvas target 1024 x 1600. Narrow straight cream gutters, maximum 4 pixels; no outer margin, no header/footer; every scene fills its own complete LANDSCAPE cell. No merged panels, insets, or changes in layout.
Style: classic 1950s-1960s Chinese small-picture storybook, early Shanghai Animation folk-art sensibility. Graceful expressive fine ink outlines, hand-painted gouache, mineral blue/green, muted cinnabar and ochre, textured warm cream paper, restrained humor and human facial expressions. Rich but legible environments; varied wide/medium/close shots. NOT modern anime, 3D, glossy or photorealistic. Ancient China, no modern objects. No words, letters, numbers, captions, speech balloons, calligraphy, watermark or symbols that look like writing ANYWHERE. Clothing and face continuity within the atlas is essential.
Characters and invariants: Tiying: young adult daughter, not a little child, simple muted rust-red robe, modest dark hair bun, determined expressive face. Chunyu Yi: mature physician father with graying beard, plain teal robe. Emperor Wen: mature man in burgundy robe and simple black Han formal cap, short beard. Plain closed bamboo petition rolls, absolutely no readable writing. No torture, mutilation, slavery service, chains, forced labor or invented release/homecoming ceremony.
Scenes in this exact order:
1. Mature Chunyu Yi stands beside an official at departure gate, plain travel bundle, worried expression, no chains or injury.
2. Exactly FIVE daughters in plain robes stand with father, youngest adult Tiying in rust-red nearest him; others muted ochre, green, gray, cream.
3. Father speaks in frustration; adult Tiying looks hurt but attentive. Keep all human and restrained, no threatening gestures.
4. Tiying in rust-red walks beside father on ancient road toward distant city, same adult face and clothes, light travel bundle.
5. Tiying kneels at a low desk preparing a plain bamboo petition; focus on determined expression, brush strokes not visible or readable.
6. Close portrait of Tiying speaking earnestly as narrator visual, holding closed petition roll; no mutilation, no imagined wounded people.
7. Tiying respectfully offers the CLOSED petition to an imperial clerk at palace entrance. No servitude scene: this is only her request.
8. Emperor Wen in burgundy thoughtfully reads plain unmarked bamboo petition in palace, expression compassionate, no direct meeting with Tiying invented.
9. Emperor consults several officials with closed bamboo legal rolls on table, indicating deliberation and order. No modern proclamation or readable text.
10. Final quiet portrait of adult Tiying holding a closed petition roll, steady hopeful expression against restrained ancient city backdrop. No father release or reunion shown.

styleRefinement.instructions: Use case: style-transfer. Restyle ONLY IMAGE 1, the edit target. IMAGE 2 (approved older 移木立信 artwork) is the PRIMARY style reference; IMAGE 3 (newly corrected fish-refusal artwork) is a SECONDARY reference for the same approved style. Do not import reference story events, characters, sword/pole/fish props, captions or text. Draw the target in the same artistic language as images 2 and 3: strongly designed Chinese folk/early Shanghai animation characters, larger expressive heads, compact stylized adult bodies, angular expressive eyebrows and noses made with very few confident strokes, small curved eyes, humorous expressive poses, fluid varied BLACK ink contours, FLAT matte pigment blocks with only spare broad ink-wash texture. Reduce realistic anatomy, skin modeling, facial shading, brocade patterns, tiny clothing folds and detailed background rendering dramatically. Robes are mostly solid muted color fields with spare trim, NO all-over elaborate embroidery. Simplify background buildings into rhythmic geometric silhouettes, light ink washes and warm UNPAINTED cream space. Restrained indigo, ochre and cinnabar, subtle paper grain like image 2, no dense brown texture overlay. NOT realistic illustrated portraiture, glossy painting, modern anime, chibi toys, 3D or photorealism. Keep all characters ADULT unless explicitly elderly. Preserve each character's consistent identifying robe color, beard and role, but redraw their form in this stylized way. No words, numerals, letters, title, captions, calligraphy, speech bubbles, watermark or readable marks ANYWHERE, including on documents, garments or props. Ignore all text visible in the style reference. Do not add a header or footer.
